evidence.field: 國語辭典書證 / 康熙字典 / 說文解字
evidence.text: The entry separately lists mouth-organ sense with the Shuowen citation; a vessel opening with a citation to Wang Chong’s Han-period 論衡·道虛; household-count uses citing 孟子 and 前漢·宣帝紀; and other senses including passage and blade edge. These citations document the cited texts, but do not date the origin of each sense or establish a semantic chain among them. Shuowen says “人所以言食也。象形”.

evidence.text: The entry labels 口 a pictogram resembling an open mouth and displays historical-form groups for Shang, Western Zhou, Warring States, Shuowen, and later traditions. It gives Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *kʰoːʔ and Mandarin kǒu. This is a secondary summary; no competing formation analysis was verified in this pass.

search_audit.outcome: Search returned an institutional paleography database, source guide, Commons oracle redraw record and secondary character entry. Opened inspected contents; the museum and character-specific Sinica pages were inaccessible or did not render.

search_audit.outcome: Found and inspected the dictionary citations for the Han-period vessel-opening example, household-count citations, Shuowen account and additional senses. No dated origin for semantic extensions was established.
Opened the exact Shang bronze description page and verified its source-record identifiers, late Shang vessel association, CC0 statement and direct Original file link.
The character-specific official Unihan URL was attempted but inaccessible in the web tool; no reading claim relies on this lookup.

gaps: The Xiaoxuetang character-specific records linked by Commons (41.E513/甲1193, 31.E4A8/late Shang vessel, and 27.53E3) did not render as readable pages in this pass. The Commons pages document their identifiers and provenance, but the underlying record images were not independently inspected.
No physical inscription or original artifact image was visually inspected. Selected examples are expressly modern vector redrawings.

Shuowen’s pictographic account is consistent with the cited oracle and bronze form tradition, but the precise graphic changes between individual examples and any corruption hypothesis are not established by the pages inspected. No supported competing formation account was found.

The Han-period vessel-opening citation documents use in that text; the exact earliest occurrence of the extended opening sense, population/counting sense, passage sense or blade-edge sense remains undetermined. The citations do not demonstrate a chronological semantic chain.

No local Unihan TSV or exact kMandarin row was inspected during this research pass; the official U+53E3 Unihan page could not be retrieved. Current Mandarin reading metadata is therefore not independently evidenced here.

No versioned local extract was created or proposed: the inspected Sinica guide permits reuse of queried glyph images and glyph-attribute information, but no extract was prepared and no separate bulk-reuse right for dictionary text was established.

limitations.text: The exact rendered files were not visually inspected in this research pass; the descriptions identify the depicted script styles and graph. Pixel-level comparison and artifact condition cannot be asserted.
